Pick over Wan 2.7 for length, audio, or video references; pick Wan 2.7 only for the cheaper short clip. Text-, image-, and reference/element-to-video, with start/end-frame control.

video.description: Text to video — generate a video from a text prompt only (no input image).

Image to video — animate a provided image as the literal FIRST FRAME — same subject, SAME framing/background, the video starts from that exact picture and moves. Use ONLY when the user wants that specific picture to come alive. Do NOT use when the subject should appear in a new scene, background, place, or action — that is element2video. This model also accepts an optional `endFrame` beside the required `startFrame`: pass both for a start-to-end frame transition that begins on the first picture and lands on the second.

Element to video — use provided image(s) as a subject/identity REFERENCE — generate NEW video footage featuring that subject, NOT locked to the input frame. The right choice for 'make a video of <this character/object/dog> doing X' and whenever the request changes the scene, background, or place (e.g. '<this dog> running in the jungle') — even if the user says 'animate' or 'make it move'. When unsure between this and image2video, pick element2video. This model accepts image, video, audio elements. To give a subject a VOICE, add an audio element (wav/mp3, 2-15s) and say in the prompt which subject speaks with it (e.g. "the woman in image 1 speaks with this voice").

models.description: PixVerse V6 — stable, natural camera and shot motion; standout 3D-anime motion scenes (surpassing Seedance 2.0 in some cases); excellent cost-performance. Text-to-video and image-to-video, with start/end-frame control.

video.description: Text to video — generate a video from a text prompt only (no input image).

Image to video — animate a provided image as the literal FIRST FRAME — same subject, SAME framing/background, the video starts from that exact picture and moves. Use ONLY when the user wants that specific picture to come alive. Do NOT use when the subject should appear in a new scene, background, place, or action — that is element2video. This model also accepts an optional `endFrame` beside the required `startFrame`: pass both for a start-to-end frame transition that begins on the first picture and lands on the second.

models.description: Smart Shot — automated shot planning. From a scene description plus optional subject references (characters, products, props) it writes a Shot Plan: a single production-design sheet with reference views, set design, a top-down camera floor plan, storyboard frames, and lighting notes. Use preview-shot-plan to see the plan alone; generate-shot-video to plan and render a video of the scene in one call.

image.description: Preview Shot Plan — produce the Shot Plan only, as a single wide image. Fast, cheap look at how the scene would be staged before committing to video. The result carries a videoPrompt and a ready-to-submit nextStep payload for rendering that exact plan into video. Pass reference images as plain URL strings (the `url` field of what successful openart_upload_import / openart_upload_pick or accepted openart_upload_metadata_get returned), NOT the whole visualReference object: subjects go in characterReferenceImageUrls (up to 3 — characters, products, props), the location in environmentReferenceImageUrl. Both are optional — a scene description alone is a complete request.

video.description: Generate Shot Video — plan the scene and render it in one call. Returns TWO assets: the video, plus the Shot Plan it was planned from. Costs the plan plus the video, so use preview-shot-plan first if the user is still exploring. Pass reference images as plain URL strings (the `url` field of what successful openart_upload_import / openart_upload_pick or accepted openart_upload_metadata_get returned), NOT the whole visualReference object: subjects go in characterReferenceImageUrls (up to 3 — characters, products, props), the location in environmentReferenceImageUrl. Both are optional — a scene description alone is a complete request.
